reason: Historical KO strength experiments used a simplified zero-gravity turn-based arena rather than the reverse-engineered Tetrp/TETR.IO synchronous authority.
Turn order changes what each side can observe before deciding and can materially affect pending-garbage safety, cancellation, downstacking, B2B/Surge, combo blocking, and pressure timing.

The exhibition integration demonstrated that the Tetrp authority can drive both bots synchronously and emit replayable .ttrm, but its initial snapshot adapter still needs correctness work before strength inference.

Tetrp replay reconstruction and deterministic engine conformance work

evidence_scope.note: Legacy-arena results remain useful priors and regression history. They are not erased, but they no longer establish strength under the target synchronous TETR.IO-like authority.

cold_clear_2: search under a fixed hard evaluator-node budget

synchronous_barrier: At a decision point, snapshot both players before either new placement is applied.
Search both sides from those snapshots.
Commit both chosen placements to the authority on the same scheduled lock frame/pace.
Only then advance attack/garbage consequences according to Tetrp engine timing.
fairness: Both players use the same match seed within a game.
Candidate and baseline use the same hard node budget and visible-state adapter.
A/A mirror control passed on tetrp-authority run 35427019103.
Slot-swap symmetry was independently demonstrated on legacy-branch migration run 35427035469; the same gate is being rerun on tetrp-authority after migration.
KO remains the only scored match outcome; APP/attack are diagnostics only.

adapter_blockers_before_strength_testing.requirement: Derive CC2 SevenBag state from already observed piece history and validated CC2 randomizer semantics. Do not infer it by naive set subtraction of current+NEXT5, and never expose hidden NEXT6+ or authority RNG state.
Verify current, hold, exactly NEXT5, board orientation, combo, B2B count/Surge state, and observable pending garbage against Tetrp authority at every decision boundary.
Preserve pending-vs-active packet timing from Tetrp. Search may model only garbage already observable to that player.
Both bots must choose before either side's newly generated attack becomes visible to the opponent.
Chosen CC2 placements must be executable under Tetrp SRS+/movement rules; path synthesis is a transport/visualization concern and must not change the chosen placement.

correctness_gates: Adapter fixture tests across 7-bag boundaries, including empty/nonempty hold.
No-hidden-information tests for NEXT6+, authority RNG, opponent board, and future attacks.
A/A deterministic symmetry controls at several seeds.
Replay round-trip validation through unmodified Tetrp reconstruction for representative short and long matches.
Trace assertions that both decisions for a lock step were produced from pre-commit snapshots.
Explicit documentation of pace and all Tetrp rule overrides for every scored run.
